comments.title: Let White take the centre
comments.text: b6 is slow: it lets White build the ideal pawn centre with d4 for free. Against this setup, striking first with d5 is the standard reply. After exd5 Qxd5 no knight can chase your queen, and you continue with Bg7.

comments.title: Challenge the strong bishop
comments.text: Bb7 is natural, but White answers d4 and takes over the centre while the light-squared bishop keeps aiming at your king side. Ba6 was more precise: after Bxa6 Nxa6 White's most dangerous piece is gone. The simple e6, blunting that bishop, was also fine.

comments.title: Develop before pushing pawns
comments.text: Pushing d4 before finishing development gives White something to attack. After cxd4 you cannot comfortably take back, because your queen side is loose and your king is still in the middle. Nc6 first was better: it develops a piece and hits White's advanced pawn.

comments.title: A cramping pawn push was on
comments.text: Rb8 defends the bishop but misses a chance. The pawn push d3 would have cramped White badly: the queen-side bishop and rook stay locked in behind their own pawn. After Rb8 White plays cxd4 and frees the position.

comments.title: Don't chase pieces to better squares
comments.text: You were clearly better, but b4 chases the knight where it wants to go: after Nc4 it eyes the hole in front of your king. Nd4 was strong, forcing trades with Nxd4 Qxd4 and leaving White's far-advanced pawn weak. When ahead, simplify and keep enemy pieces passive.

comments.title: A cool-headed retreat
comments.text: Well played. With White's knight attacking your bishop, the natural Qd7 runs into Nxb7 and costs material, and the greedy cxb2 lets White take over with Rxc5. The calm retreat Ba8 keeps the bishop on the long diagonal and holds the balance. Few players at your level find it.

comments.title: Recapture first
comments.text: White had just taken a knight, and it had to be taken back: Bxc6 keeps material level. Instead cxb2 attacks the rook, but it simply steps away with Rxc5, and White stays a piece up with your corner bishop still attacked. Recapture first, then look for extras.

comments.title: Seek counterplay when behind
comments.text: Already in trouble, you needed counterplay. Qb6 hits the rook and keeps your far-advanced passed pawn as a real threat; after Bxa8 Qxc5 the fight goes on. Bxc6 followed by Rxc6 just trades pieces while a piece down, which makes White's job easy.

lessons.title: Fight for the centre early
lessons.text: Twice in the opening a slow wing move let White take the centre for free. Meet a slow setup with an immediate central pawn break.

lessons.title: Finish development first
lessons.text: A pawn push before your pieces were out gave White targets, and a rook move missed a cramping pawn advance. Count developed pieces before committing pawns.

lessons.title: Recapture, then look for more
lessons.text: The game turned when you ignored a capture to chase a rook. When a piece is taken, take back first unless you have calculated something better to the end.
